To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Hamiltonian for the Maxwell field on the null surface is the energy, the Hamiltonian for a scalar field on a null surface is the total energy plus the energy of the field, and that the commutation relations on a null surface are the same as in Minkowski space.

the Hamiltonian for the electromagnetic field on an outgoing null surface plus the energy radiated is the total energy of the system, that the Hamiltonian gives once-integrated field equation, and that the commutation relations for field strengths are i times the appropriate Dirac bracket.
the Hamiltonian for the electromagnetic field is the total energy and that the Dirac bracket is the commutator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of the Hamiltonian for a dynamical field on a characteristic surface.
the construction of the canonical Hamiltonian formalism for the electromagnetic field on a null cone.
the construction of the Hamiltonian for a scalar or electromagnetic field on the outgoing null cone plus the portion of space-like infinity that extends back to the past null cone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Dirac brackets are the commutators of the fields on the null cone plus.
the Dirac brackets for the electromagnetic field on an outgoing null hypersurface are the commutators of the field strengths.
the canonical formalism on a characteristic surface provides a powerful tool for the analysis and solution of field problems on null surfaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hamiltonian formulation of the field theory on a null surface is a natural generalization of the standard Hamiltonian formalism for field theories on space-like surfaces.

a Hamiltonian formulation has been set up for the scalar and the electromagnetic field on a characteristic surface and that the Hamiltonian yields the once-integrated dynamical equations for the field variables.
the Hamiltonian for the field theory on a null surface is the energy radiated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of the electromagnetic field, there are only two constraints, and they are the usual gauge conditions, so that no further constraints need be imposed on the field variables.
the Dirac brackets for the dynamical fields are identical to the Poisson brackets.

, in a theory with constraints on a characteristic surface (in the case of the scalar field, this is the outgoing null cone; for the electromagnetic field, it is a portion of the outgoing null cone plus the portion of the null cone extending back to space-like infinities), the Dirac brackets are a necessary ingredient for the Hamiltonian to be the total energy.
